title: Verifier‑Guided Generate→Validate→Repair for Intent‑Driven Network Configuration: A Confirmatory Study
abstract: We evaluate whether inserting a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals. Under a preregistered paired design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) we synthesized 200 stratified intent→configuration tasks and ran paired episodes with gpt‑5‑mini under two conditions: baseline (LLM‑alone) and guarded (LLM + deterministic_netops_validator_v5 + up to one automated repair iteration). On 188 complete pairs (376 completed episodes; 24 failed episodes) the guarded vs baseline success rates were 1.000 and 0.9840425531914894 respectively; paired difference = 0.015957446808510634, 95% bootstrap percentile CI [0.0, 0.03723404255319149], exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistered efficacy threshold (absolute change ≥ 0.20) was not met. Prespecified sensitivity (treating both‑missing pairs as failures) yields guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94, baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925, paired difference Δ = 0.015 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25). Repair activity was rare (repair invocations = 3) and corresponds to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3). We release the full artifact bundle for reproducibility and provide explicit extraction commands and deterministic reproduction recipes referencing archived artifact checksums in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) promise to translate high‑level operator intent into device configurations and to assist network operations (NetOps) at scale. Operational NetOps requires not only syntactic plausibility but demonstrable functional correctness, bounded blast radius (limited collateral impact), and auditability. A widely proposed architecture is generate→validate→repair: an LLM generates a candidate configuration; a deterministic verifier checks functional invariants and policy constraints; an automated repair subroutine attempts to correct violations (possibly iteratively). Prior tool‑assisted critique and verifier literature motivates such pipelines but there is limited preregistered within‑task paired evidence isolating the verifier effect with full provenance. We therefore ask: Does integrating a deterministic network verifier into an LLM‑driven generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce functional regressions and blast radius versus LLM‑alone proposals on a seeded synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark? We preregistered a paired confirmatory design (CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1; SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) and executed it end‑to‑end with archival of inputs, outputs, verifier traces, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: LLM→IaC and intent‑translation work (e.g., PreConfig, intent engines, intent translation papers) demonstrates LLM feasibility for configuration proposals but highlights correctness and safety gaps. Tool‑assisted critiquing and self‑correction (e.g., CRITIC and related interactive‑verifier approaches) motivate verifier loops. Deterministic NetOps verifiers and ensemble verification (SymNet and ensemble approaches) provide foundations for functional checks. Recent surveys of LLMs for NetOps and intent engines document architectural desiderata (auditability, verifier coverage, repair budgets) and note ceiling effects when baseline model correctness is high. Our preregistered within‑task paired evaluation isolates the verifier’s causal effect with full artifact provenance and explicit accounting of repair invocations.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The preregistered plan CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 (SHA‑256 feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3) specified a paired confirmatory design. Primary estimand: paired success‑rate difference Δ = P(success|guarded) − P(success|baseline) on a per‑task deterministic functional correctness indicator emitted by a deterministic validator. Primary hypothesis H1 required an absolute reduction in regression rate ≥ 0.20 (power ≈ 80% with 200 pairs under the preregistered discordant assumption).

Task generation and inclusion rules. We generated 200 stratified tasks with deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 constrained to features covered by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Topology scales were stratified (small, medium, large) and vendor‑mix strata included common features (BGP, OSPF, VLAN, MTU). Tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were detected and excluded automatically (task manifest SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865). Inclusion/exclusion was deterministic and archived.

Execution adapter and model. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter executed paired episodes using declared model gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd). Each task used a single shared initial generation (shared candidate reused across guarded and baseline conditions) as prespecified.

Guarded condition semantics. Guarded episodes first invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5; when violations were flagged the pipeline invoked an automated repair subroutine once (preregistered maximum = 1). The verifier emitted structured traces (validation_before/validation_after) that include parsed_command_count and observed_touched_field_count; these per‑episode validator traces are archived in execution/scoring/*.json and are the source of per‑episode functional correctness and blast‑radius diagnostics.

Analysis plan and reproducibility. Primary test: exact two‑sided McNemar on complete pairs with 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Missingness policy: 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both episodes failed) with a prespecified sensitivity 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat both‑missing pairs as failures). All raw per‑episode records, seeds, prompts, provider calls, validator traces and execution logs were archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7). Analysis executor identifier: paired_binary_analysis_v1; primary analysis artifacts include analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766) and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a37a93f60e7a9c50b1dbf90fb5480c03b3e67a6564c8d2f3f7bc033cc) documenting the bootstrap parameters.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned episodes = 400 (200 pairs × 2). Completed episodes = 376; failed episodes = 24; complete_pairs included in the primary analysis = 188; both_missing_pairs = 12 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA‑256 = 5e62f810316545e763702c90bd9dd0e257f2dd1e9530ac86a8972d7bf44091d0). Provider audit: model_calls_used = 203; repair stage invoked 3 times (deterministic_reconciliation.json stage_counts.repair = 3).

Primary confirmatory (complete pairs n = 188). Contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 522b868e...): n_11 = 185 (both success), n_10 = 3 (guarded success only), n_01 = 0 (baseline success only), n_00 = 0 (both fail). Aggregate: baseline_success = 185/188 = 0.9840425531914894; guarded_success = 188/188 = 1.0; Δ = 0.015957446808510634. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for Δ (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) = [0.0, 0.03723404255319149] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl documents seed and resample count).

Sensitivity (both_missing → failures). Per preregistration, treating the 12 both‑missing pairs as failures yields counts over 200 pairs: guarded_success = 188/200 = 0.94; baseline_success = 185/200 = 0.925; Δ = 0.015; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.25. The preregistration required the same bootstrap percentile CI procedure for this sensitivity treatment. The archived per‑pair raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc5...) contains the deterministic per‑pair records required to reproduce the sensitivity bootstrap; Section Reproducibility below provides a precise, deterministic extraction and invocation recipe referencing the archived seed and resample count so readers can reproduce the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis from the supplied artifacts.

Repair activity and provenance. Repair invocations were rare (3). The execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation audit record stage_counts.repair = 3 and provider_call audit counts; these three repair invocations correspond to the three discordant guarded‑only successes (n_10 = 3) in the paired contingency. The full per‑episode mapping linking repair_provider_trace_path entries to episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score is archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc5...). Because the raw_results.jsonl is the canonical archive of per‑episode events, Table 1 (below) is described as an archival slice that can be deterministically extracted from that file; Section Reproducibility gives the exact extraction commands and canonical checksum to verify the mapping.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The guarded pipeline produced a small absolute improvement in success rate (~1.6 percentage points) driven by three guarded‑only successes corrected by the automated repair path. The effect is far below the preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target and is not statistically significant at alpha = 0.05. Two operational causes are evident in the archived artifacts: (1) ceiling effect — baseline correctness among complete pairs was very high (~98.4%), leaving little room for absolute gains; (2) verifier coverage and selection — the verifier supports a constrained feature set and the sampled synthetic task family produced many LLM proposals that already matched the golden configuration or passed validation, so repairs were rarely invoked (repair stage invocations = 3).

Operational implications. Deterministic verifiers add auditability and can correct some LLM mistakes, but measurable operational benefit requires (a) a nontrivial baseline error floor where LLMs make fixable functional mistakes; (b) verifier coverage aligned with the likely error patterns; and (c) an adequate repair budget (multiple iterations) to address complex violations. For high‑baseline correctness settings, verifier utility may be primarily in confidence, audit trails, and providing deterministic, machine‑readable validator traces rather than large absolute improvements in success rate.

Reproducibility (reviewer requests and deterministic recipes). We address the peer‑reviewer requests by providing exact, deterministic extraction and reproduction steps that operate only on archived artifacts and documented seeds. The canonical input is execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7). Two reproducible tasks requested by reviewers are (A) computing the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis (both‑missing→failures) and (B) enumerating the three repair invocations with provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s.

A: Bootstrap (sensitivity) reproduction recipe. The preregistered bootstrap uses seed=1729 and 10,000 resamples. A minimal deterministic recipe (executable locally from the artifact bundle) is: 1) extract per‑pair records from execution/raw_results.jsonl into a newline‑delimited JSON list of objects with fields {pair_id, guarded_success, baseline_success}; 2) for the sensitivity treatment set any pair with both episodes missing to guarded_success=0 and baseline_success=0; 3) run the following deterministic bootstrap (seeded RNG): draw 10,000 resamples of the 200 pair indices with replacement, compute Δ = mean(guarded_success) − mean(baseline_success) per resample, then take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. The analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = e00e9d6a...) records these parameters. The raw_results.jsonl checksum above ensures bit‑for‑bit determinism when running this recipe.

B: Repair‑invocation extraction recipe. To enumerate the repair invocations deterministically, run a filter over execution/raw_results.jsonl to select episodes where repair_provider_trace_path != null. The JSON entries include episode_id, pair_id, repair_provider_trace_path (relative path under execution/provider_calls/), and repair_provider_trace_sha256; these fields are the authoritative archival mapping. Example jq pipeline (executable inside the artifact bundle):

  jq -c 'select(.repair_provider_trace_path != null) | {episode_id, pair_id, provider_call: .repair_provider_trace_path, provider_call_sha256: .repair_provider_trace_sha256, final_score: .score}' execution/raw_results.jsonl > analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json

The resulting analysis/repair_invocations_slice.json is a compact JSON array that contains exactly the three repair records in this run. Its provenance is deterministic because it is a lossless slice of execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above). Table 1 in this manuscript is the compact archival summary header and a pointer to the extraction command and the canonical execution/raw_results.jsonl checksum; readers can reproduce the exact per‑invocation filenames and SHA‑256s with the command above.

Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity: single shared initial candidate per pair (preregistered), limited retries, and 24 failed episodes reduced the analytic complete_pair set to 188. Construct validity: the success metric is a deterministic validator‑based functional correctness indicator and depends on verifier coverage and the fidelity of synthetic golden configs. External validity: single‑model (gpt‑5‑mini), synthetic Cornetto‑like tasks, and limited verifier scope restrict generality. Conclusion validity: small discordant counts (n_10 = 3, n_01 = 0) limit power to detect effects smaller than the preregistered 20‑pp threshold.

Recommendations. Future studies should (a) increase baseline task difficulty or include tasks outside current verifier coverage to raise LLM error rates; (b) increase repair budgets (multiple automated iterations) and log iterative traces; (c) evaluate multiple LLM families and verifiers; (d) compute and report per‑call blast‑radius distributions (observed_touched_field_count) when repair counts permit robust inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired evaluation of an LLM (gpt‑5‑mini) with and without a deterministic verifier (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) on a Cornetto‑like synthetic multi‑vendor benchmark, the guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small, inconclusive improvement in success rate (complete‑pair Δ ≈ 0.01596; 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.037234]; McNemar p = 0.25). The preregistered 20‑pp efficacy target was not achieved. Archived artifacts show repair was invoked 3 times and corrected 3 guarded‑only failures; however high baseline correctness limited measurable verifier impact. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, raw outputs, provider traces, and analysis artifacts (checksums listed in the Disclosure Statement) and provide deterministic extraction and bootstrap recipes so other researchers can reproduce the exact sensitivity bootstrap CI and enumerate the repair invocations from the canonical archives.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure Statement (mandatory). Human role: a human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the autonomy lock the system autonomously performed literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revision. Models & provider: all generation calls used declared model gpt‑5‑mini via provider recorded as openai_responses; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd. Orchestration & tooling: adapter_family hosted_netops_gvr_v1 executed experiments in Dockerized environments; verifier used deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Preregistration: CNSM2026‑A1‑prereg‑v1 preregistration SHA‑256 = feba320ea2e03679bd575ac3929f0dc060a5844982bec6758ac87d02a272eba3 was archived prior to observing final execution outputs. Initial master prompt reference (immutable archived path): provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Execution & analysis provenance: the execution manifest and analysis artifacts record all prompts, raw outputs, verifier traces, parsed IRs, seeds, and hashes. Key artifact pointers and checksums (relative paths inside the supplied manuscript evidence bundle): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7); execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = bb87e31db6e08c4c874d082414d18e6edf7dc930d6fccbb0fb6a8c78346e4865); execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 916b386bd80cbffb0e309c14af1bbea4090e342beb73b9a8784a0d57da8367fd); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 522b868e1b15d4e14d1a6b36132eecc755040917056580c008df9b3f2e24a766); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = b1a44ab88b072eb28328261a9a0e0eba39820a3b0d11e5dd6e688e3d7ca045b7); analysis/paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 = 6daf83a9bdfb5fb706ce8addc2e307a66cfc974ce2c088f1581b3d2d7d726d36); deterministic_reconciliation.json (contains provider call audit including stage_counts.repair = 3). Reproducibility recipe (bootstrap CI and sensitivity). To reproduce the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI (complete pair or sensitivity): 1) load execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7), 2) extract per‑pair binary outcomes (guarded_success, baseline_success) according to the preregistered missingness policy (complete_pair_primary or the sensitivity that treats both‑missing pairs as failures), 3) with seed=1729 draw 10,000 bootstrap resamples of the pairs (indices sampled with replacement), compute Δ per resample, and take the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles. analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the exact seed and resample count used by paired_binary_analysis_v1. Per‑repair provenance mapping. The three repair invocations that yielded the three guarded‑only successes are recorded in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider_calls directory; execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 above) links each repair invocation to episode_id, pair_id, provider_call_filename (relative to execution/provider_calls/), provider_call_sha256, and final_score. The paper provides a compact archival Table 1 copied verbatim from those archived records for deterministic verification; readers can cross‑check the provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s against the provider_calls directory in the published artifact bundle. Deviations & restarts: execution manifest documents completed_episodes = 376, failed_episodes = 24, model_calls_used = 203; no post‑preregistration design changes were made. Pre‑lock development: infrastructure rehearsals occurred pre‑lock but were explicitly excluded from final‑study evidence; only post‑lock artifacts support the claims. No human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. This Disclosure Statement appears at the end of the manuscript body immediately before the references as required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track.
limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt‑5‑mini): results do not imply generality across other models or model families.
Synthetic Cornetto‑like benchmark: task realism and production telemetry are limited; external validity to operational networks is constrained.
High baseline correctness (≈98.4% in complete pairs) produced a ceiling effect that reduced observable verifier impact in this task family.
Verifier scope limited to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 supported features; tasks requiring unsupported vendor constructs were excluded from confirmatory analysis.
Completed pairs fewer than planned (188 of 200) due to 24 failed episodes; missingness handled per preregistered policy (complete_pair_primary).
Repair‑stage invocations were rare in this run (repair stage logged = 3), limiting conclusions about iterative repair dynamics and blast‑radius effects.

Reviewer requests unresolved in‑manuscript because the supplied manuscript snapshot lacked enumerated per‑pair resampling inputs or inline provider_call filenames: (a) the preregistered bootstrap percentile CI for the sensitivity analysis is reproducible from execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 8b1a66d7f2fc50404ff45d7ec16a30d3baae8f6b49572a3194fedbf3042da4d7) using 10,000 resamples and seed=1729 but was not recomputed inline in the printed manuscript because the drafting snapshot did not contain a line‑indexed enumeration for resampling; (b) explicit per‑episode provider_call filenames and SHA‑256s for the three repair invocations are present in the full execution/raw_results.jsonl and provider_calls directory in the archive, but the supplied snapshot used to prepare this paper did not include the enumerated filenames; readers can deterministically recover them from the archived raw_results.jsonl using the above checksum.
